raw_response:
I've been working this land for 55 years. I know what Quzhou asks of me — dry springs, hot summers, cold winters. My 30 mu runs wheat in winter and maize in summer on the same ground. That's how we've always done it here on the North China Plain, and it works.

For wheat, I plant every October after the maize comes off. I'll rotary till the stubble under — I've done it every year, keeps the soil loose. I use the improved variety the extension office brought in a while back — better than the old stuff, holds up against the rust. I put down base fertilizer before planting — compound fertilizer with some urea — then topdress at jointing. Three irrigations: one before winter sets in, one at jointing, one at grain fill. Two rounds of pesticide — one herbicide early, one for aphids and powdery mildew near heading. I expect around 450 jin per mu on a decent year.

For maize, I direct seed right after wheat harvest in June — no time to waste and my back isn't what it was. I use hybrid seed, same variety I've been using for years, 郑单958 type. Summer rains help but I have the well ready. I'll irrigate twice if the season is dry. One pesticide pass for corn borer. Maize gets more nitrogen — it needs it. I should pull 550 jin or so.

Some of my sons work in town, so I keep things manageable. 30 mu I can handle myself mostly, with help at harvest.
